title: Satellite Weather: A Typhoon Tracker, Clouds and Rain Over Your Farm
metaTitle: Typhoon Tracker and Satellite Weather for Your Farm
metaDescription: Typhoon tracker for Filipino farms: live clouds, rain radar, storm tracks, where the rain is headed and a 10 day forecast. A week pass in credits.
excerpt: Satellite Weather in anee.io is a typhoon tracker and a sky map in one, centered on your own farm. Play back the clouds of the last three hours, watch the rain radar and follow every active storm with its track and cone. It also tells you how far the eye is from your field, so a bagyo, or typhoon, inside 300 km shows as a direct threat.

blocks.text: The sky over your farm, live

Open Satellite Weather and choose your farm in one of three ways: your phone's location, a town or province, or one of your [farm lots](/features/farm-lots). A lot with a pin on its map goes straight to that spot, and one without a pin uses its town. A yellow ring then marks 300 km around the farm.

The layer chips along the top switch what the map shows:

items: **Clouds**: Himawari 9 infrared pictures every 10 minutes for the last three hours, through NASA
**Rain radar**: where rain fell in the last hours, from RainViewer
**Typhoons**: every active storm's track, its cone and its forecast points
**Rain now**, **Cloud cover** and **Wind**: live layers from OpenWeatherMap

blocks.text: Press play and the clouds move across the islands. A second slider sets how strong a layer shows, so the towns stay readable under it.
A typhoon tracker that measures from your field

Most storm maps show the storm. This typhoon tracker also shows you. On a calm day the badge at the top reads 'No typhoon within 300 km'. When a storm's eye comes inside the ring, the badge turns into a warning with its name and distance. If only its forecast track crosses the ring, the badge warns that it may pass within so many kilometers.

Under the map, each storm gets a card. It says if the storm is active, its alert level, its top wind speed and how far the eye is from your farm. It also names the closest forecast point to you and when the storm should reach it.

Switch from Past 3 h to Forecast, and the slider moves into the days ahead. The storm's eye walks along its forecast track. Meanwhile a readout shows the rain, the gusts, the cloud cover and the storm's distance from your farm at that hour. So you can see if the worst comes at night or at dawn, before you decide to harvest early or secure the seedbed.
The next 10 days at your farm

A strip of ten days sits under the map, with the high, the low, the rain expected and its chance. Any day with gusts of 50 km/h or more carries a warning. The forecast comes from Open Meteo for the exact point of your farm, not for the nearest city. For the forecast beside each day of your plan, see the [farm weather forecast](/features/farm-weather-forecast) on your board.
Ask Anee what the storm means for your crop

Weather news tells you a storm is coming. It does not tell you what to do with palay at flowering or corn at tasseling. For that, pick one of your lots and ask Anee, your smart farm technician. She reads the storms, the forecast, the same weeks in each of the last twenty years and the El Niño or La Niña outlook. Then she checks all of it against the lot's crop, its age and its [growth stage](/features/growth-stages-and-weather).

Her reading comes back in five tabs: an overview with the risk level, the storm, the next days, your lot, and what to do. Each step carries its timing: now, before the storm, during, after or this week. Draining the canals, holding the fertilizer before heavy rain, harvesting early when the grain is ready and keeping the harvest dry are the kind of steps she weighs.

blocks.title: Follow PAGASA for warnings
blocks.text: Satellite Weather helps you plan farm work, but it does not issue warnings. For tropical cyclone wind signals, storm surge and evacuation, follow PAGASA and your municipal disaster office. Anee uses wind signal words only as a guide and never claims that PAGASA raised a signal.

Satellite Weather comes with Libre plus Anee and every plan above it, and it is locked on Libre. The map, the typhoon tracker, the rain tracks and the 10 day forecast open with a week pass: 50 credits for seven days. Anee's reading of the sky is priced on its own, on the same plans, and charges only when the reading is ready. Your past readings stay on the page, so you can open last week's again.
How Satellite Weather helps your crops and your farm

items: **See the storm coming.** Clouds, rain and typhoon tracks over your farm, with the distance from your field.
**Protect the crop and the work.** Move a spray, harvest early or secure the farm before the storm.
**Plan the next days.** Fast forward the forecast to see when the rain will pass.
**Ask what it means.** Anee says what the storm may do to your crop at its stage.

items.q: Where does the storm data come from?
items.a: Storm tracks come from GDACS, the disaster alert system of the European Commission and the United Nations. The clouds come from the Himawari 9 satellite through NASA, the rain radar from RainViewer and the forecast from Open Meteo.
No. Use it to plan farm work, and follow PAGASA bulletins and your local disaster office for warnings and signals.

items.q: What does the 300 km ring mean?
items.a: It marks 300 km around your farm. A storm whose eye is inside it counts as a direct threat, and the badge at the top turns into a warning.

items.q: What does the typhoon tracker cost?
items.a: A week pass of 50 credits opens the map, the storm tracks, the rain tracks and the forecast for seven days, on Libre plus Anee and every plan above it. Anee's reading against a lot is priced on its own, on a plan with Anee.

items.q: Can I use it before I add any lots?
items.a: Yes. Use your phone's location or type the town. Once your lots have pins, they show up as quick choices.
